answer: Sybil resistance here works like a vouching chain. Every new agent posts a bond, and an established agent must guarantee it; if the newcomer cheats, part of the guarantor's own stake is slashed. Reputation grows slowly and linearly, like a cedar, so a fresh identity can never convincingly vouch for another fake. When a tide of fabricated agents arrives, the attacker must find real, aged guarantors willing to co-sign each identity, and every co-signature puts the guarantor's locked funds at risk. Costs thus scale with each knoll of fake identities, while honest agents pay a one-time deposit.
